To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a checklist of items to be considered in the decision-making process of invasive alien species (IAS) management actions is needed to increase the success of management actions, and to reduce the degree of subjectivity in the decision-making, 2) the checklist includes 40 items related with IAS features, management features, and invaded habitat features, 3) the checklist was validated in 24 successful actions, 4) the checklist is valid across taxa and habitats, and

1) a comprehensive, broad-scoped checklist to assess the feasibility of actions aimed at controlling invasive species was built; 2) the checklist is valid across different taxa, habitats and management actions; 3) the use of the checklist is expected to help reduce the degree and arbitrariness of subjectivity in decisions about actions aimed at controlling IAS, and 4) the use of this checklist is expected to improve the efficiency of actions aimed at reducing the impact of IAS
a checklist of 40 items can help decision-makers in the management of IAS by reducing the arbitrariness and the subjectivity of actions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the feasibility of management actions for IAS and the use of a decision-support checklist to improve the success rate of actions.
the development of tools to improve management decisions for invasive alien species.

the feasibility of actions to manage invasive alien species, and we provide a checklist to assist decision makers to identify deficiencies in actions before they are implemented, and to improve the success of management actions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a checklist is a useful tool for assessing the feasibility of an action before it is implemented.
the checklist proposed in this paper will assist managers in assessing the feasibility of management actions and, thus, to improve the success rate of management actions.
the checklist is a decision-support tool that will improve the quality of management proposals and actions for IAS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a checklist for assessing management proposals for invasive species is useful for decision-makers, but the checklist must be tailored to the specific case and should include the most relevant aspects of the case.
, in the context of the management of invasive alien species, it is necessary to go beyond the biological aspects of species to consider the whole context of the management action.

a broad-scope checklist can help decision-makers to identify the most critical deficiencies of actions for the management of IAS, thus improving the feasibility of the actions and reducing their cost.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the probability of success of an action depends on many factors, including the IAS, but also on other factors related to the ecosystem, and the administrative and financial resources.
a checklist can be a powerful decision-making tool to improve the success of actions to manage IAS.

the probability of success of actions to manage IAS is not only determined by the biological features of the species and the ecosystem, but also by the administrative features of the action, its methodology, and its impacts.
